Quick prep brief
Purpose of the meeting
The session is to kick off enhancements review and sizing for Sprint 2, specifically to check whether the team has enough information from the**“Must Have” tickets** and decide what can be reviewed/sized now versus what needs further clarification.
Review priority
[Re: [Review] Enhancements & Sizing](https://outlook.office365.com/owa/?ItemID=AAMkADAwMDY5M2RlLWQ4YTgtNDk0ZC05NjE0LWY5NDM4ODY2NjlmYwBGAAAAAADj6PLKElMiQqCITvdyZx6EBwBDVw5BF5KXS4J9nmOzC999AAAAAAEMAABDVw5BF5KXS4J9nmOzC999AAAe0PAnAAA%3d&exvsurl=1&viewmodel=ReadMessageItem&EntityRepresentationId=0acdfd83-0979-4cb1-a0eb-f17f8d59b5b0) says the meeting will review the https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-24?search_id=8285876f-f3cc-436f-9943-85be8017d2e1 in this order: Must Have’s not yet sized first, then Should Have’s, then Could Have’s.
What you should have ready
Come in with a sizing lens across these effort areas: BA effort, QA / SIT effort, Front End effort if any, Back End effort if any, and Architecture effort if any.
Given your frontend lead role on Zimmermann, I’d focus your prep on this simple mental model:

For each enhancement:
1. Is there any Front End impact?
2. Is the requirement clear enough to size?
3. Does it touch PWA Kit / React, Contentful, SFCC integration, checkout, account, PDP/PLP, or CMS-rendered areas?
4. Are there design/Figma dependencies?
5. Are there API/backend dependencies?
6. Is this a pure FE change, shared FE/BE change, or needs architecture input?
7. Can we size now, or do we need clarification?

Suggested stance for the meeting
You can frame your input like this:

For FE sizing, I’ll separate the tickets into:
- Clear enough to size now
- Needs design clarification
- Needs API/backend clarification
- Needs architecture decision
- No obvious FE impact
For anything touching UI, I’ll also call out whether the designs/design system are mature enough for us to size confidently, or whether we need assumptions documented before committing.

Questions worth asking
Use these if the discussion gets fuzzy:

* “Do we have enough acceptance criteria to size this, or should this go into clarification first?”
* “Is the expected UI already covered in Figma, or are we sizing based on assumptions?”
* “Is this enhancement purely frontend, or does it need backend/API support?”
* “Are we sizing implementation only, or also discovery/spike effort?”
* “Should we capture assumptions separately so the estimate doesn’t look more certain than it is?”
* “For Must Haves, do we need a minimum viable implementation for Sprint 2, or the full desired enhancement?”

Quick sizing template you can use live

Ticket:
Priority: Must / Should / Could
FE impact: Yes / No / Unknown
FE estimate:
BE dependency:
QA/SIT consideration:
Design dependency:
Architecture input needed: Yes / No
Clarifications required:
Sizing confidence: High / Medium / Low
Recommendation: Size now / Clarify first / Spike needed

People context
Required invitees include [Linsangan, Gideon R.](https://www.office.com/search?q=Linsangan%2c+Gideon+R.&EntityRepresentationId=a09dcabc-7f11-42fd-a47a-081c6e8e53ba), [Navarro, Marcel Angelo N.](https://www.office.com/search?q=Navarro%2c+Marcel+Angelo+N.&EntityRepresentationId=c6464783-afc3-4afa-825c-43fcb4a494af), [Chaloner, Isabel](https://www.office.com/search?q=Chaloner%2c+Isabel&EntityRepresentationId=00f4faa0-050a-4d4b-9880-6d9aa4b15b83), [Tsang, Jasmijn](https://www.office.com/search?q=Tsang%2c+Jasmijn&EntityRepresentationId=4c02c6a5-38bd-40a8-9378-35ffab98147a), [Ramachandran, Manikandan](https://www.office.com/search?q=Ramachandran%2c+Manikandan&EntityRepresentationId=ab53e6fe-d92b-4c59-bd50-14111a7f060d), and [Crisostomo, Victor T.](https://www.office.com/search?q=Crisostomo%2c+Victor+T.&EntityRepresentationId=c0b202e9-ee0d-435c-a543-8f5adfae31a7); optional invitees include [Lucy Fu](https://www.office.com/search?q=Lucy+Fu&EntityRepresentationId=6ede0339-cd04-4981-a1f3-6bf772481b29), [Rebecca Jourdan](https://www.office.com/search?q=Rebecca+Jourdan&EntityRepresentationId=18f5fd67-819f-4248-86db-b543d4364d7b), [Lavelle, Tim](https://www.office.com/search?q=Lavelle%2c+Tim&EntityRepresentationId=488f1fe0-33fb-4ab4-894e-9975ee7dca86), [Emma Kirwan](https://www.office.com/search?q=Emma+Kirwan&EntityRepresentationId=3f4610bd-c3ed-4f2f-b315-990a2231f15e), [Dani Rivett](https://www.office.com/search?q=Dani+Rivett&EntityRepresentationId=96ef42b2-8d8e-4bc2-938c-e036c26501f2), [Pagaduan, Jesse C.](https://www.office.com/search?q=Pagaduan%2c+Jesse+C.&EntityRepresentationId=15655688-6c9a-497e-97a1-d6500c999816), and [Cacalda, Hazel Marie](https://www.office.com/search?q=Cacalda%2c+Hazel+Marie&EntityRepresentationId=d1603ce6-a1dc-4b31-979b-29690c1c3ca5).
Your likely contribution
I’d go in ready to be the person who keeps the sizing grounded: call out where FE effort is straightforward, where UI/design maturity affects confidence, and where integration/backend clarification is needed before anyone treats an estimate as firm. That should help the team move through the Must Haves without overcommitting on under-specified tickets.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

1	# PRD – Data Migration, SEO, GEO & URL
2	
3	*Last updated: 2026-06-11*
4	
5	Scope: Magento→SFCC data migration, URL strategy and redirects, SEO (canonicals/hreflang, sitemaps/robots, rendering/headings/meta, structured data), and GEO routing foundations. Regional storefront routing, consent, and currency live in [regional.md](regional.md).
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Data Migration (DMU-001 – DMU-012)
10	
11	- Product feed via MuleSoft from AP21 to SFCC covering ~1,600 active SKUs: names, descriptions, attributes, imagery refs, category assignments (DMU-001). Ongoing product sync via MuleSoft post-migration. **DMU-002 — Confirmed (status flipped from Ready for Sign Off, 2026-06-11).** The PWA-side contract is settled: SFCC displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for product data (JT 04-06), with AP21 as the master of record. Upstream sourcing (the first load draws from **both AP21 and PLM** via MuleSoft, with Magento-enriched data migrated after the initial load) sits **outside the PWA boundary** — the PWA does not enrich or compute product attributes itself, it renders the MuleSoft payload. The earlier RJ challenges (PLM/Magento enrichment) are upstream-of-MuleSoft concerns, not PWA blockers.
12	- Multi-region catalogue assignments and regional merchandising preserved across all storefronts (DMU-003).
13	- Registered customer records (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-25): **only email address and Omneo ID** are migrated to SFCC. Name, phone number, saved delivery addresses, and communication preferences are sourced **live from Omneo at login**, not held in SFCC. The previously requested 20-address cap is no longer relevant (addresses are not stored in SFCC). FE must treat Omneo as the source of customer profile data post-login; degrade gracefully if Omneo is unreachable.
14	- **Customer passwords are not migrated** — customers must reset on first login (DMU-005). See AGENTS.md "Magento password migration" gotcha.
15	- Saved payment card details are **not** migrated; customers re-enter at next purchase (DMU-006).
16	- Historical order records are **not** migrated into SFCC. Order history is accessed via NewStore **through MuleSoft** where customer identifiers match across online and in-store channels (DMU-007, **Confirmed 2026-06-11** — status flipped from Ready for Sign Off). The PWA displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for customer order history (JT 04-06); no order data is held in SFCC. ⚠️ Source-of-truth flag retained: the requirement text + JT name **NewStore via MuleSoft**, while an RJ comment says **"Order history will come from Omneo"** — the upstream source (NewStore vs Omneo behind MuleSoft) is out of the PWA boundary but remains unreconciled; see Open Items. For the ME storefront, only online orders appear in My Account order history; the orders API returns the most recent 50 orders held in NewStore, and until NewStore transitions in ME only online orders are visible — no FE customisation required to filter retail orders (DMU-008, Ready for Sign Off 2026-05-25).
17	- Contentful API connections reconfigured to point at the new platform; no bulk content re-entry needed (DMU-009, **challenged → Open** — RJ: no longer required as AS will be setting up Contentful; reconciliation pending). Mechanism note: Contentful integrates as the headless CMS via the **Salesforce App Exchange connector**, consuming content through the Contentful **delivery API** for all customer-facing pages across all storefronts (Third Party Integrations: CMS / Contentful) — i.e. the integration is the App Exchange connector, not a bespoke API rewire.
18	- Product images and digital assets (DMU-010, de-scoped 2026-05-25): **out of scope for migration.** Images and assets are stored and served from Contentful — there is no CDN migration, no asset URL rewrite, and no 301 redirects for asset URLs. ### Template delivery scope (Storefront Templates sheet)
The system delivers page templates for the homepage, global navigation, footer, and country/language selector. (Catalogue, cart/checkout, account, content/static, and SEO-migration templates are covered in their own PRDs.)

---

## 1. Global Header (HPC-015 – HPC-028)

- **Rotating promotional announcement banner** above the header — CMS-managed via Contentful (HPC-017, confirmed).

### Header icons (HPC-018 — Confirmed)
The confirmed header icon set is: **Search, Account, and Bag** (HPC-018). Locate Boutique, Contact Us, and Newsletter are **not part of the header** — confirmed per design review on 23 June 2026. Placement of those three icons elsewhere (footer or other location) remains design-dependent and will follow the new UX designs.
